en: Typhoon Haiyan, known locally as Yolanda, struck the Philippines in 2013 as one of the strongest tropical cyclones ever recorded.
The rich volcanic soil around Mount Mayon in Albay makes the area highly fertile for growing abaca and coconut trees.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol are made of thousands of cone-shaped limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the South China Sea.
Olympus Mons on Mars is the largest known volcano in the solar system, standing about three times taller than Mount Everest.
Sirius, located in the Canis Major constellation, is the brightest star visible in the night sky from Earth.
Astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed the Apollo 11 spacecraft in the Moon's Mare Tranquillitatis, or Sea of Tranquility.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines injected massive amounts of sulfur dioxide into the atmosphere, temporarily cooling global temperatures.
The Valley Fault System is a major earthquake hazard in the Philippines, stretching across several provinces including Metro Manila.
Italian scientist Evangelista Torricelli invented the mercury barometer in 1643 to measure atmospheric pressure and predict weather changes.
NASA's Magellan spacecraft used radar to map ninety-eight percent of the surface of Venus during its mission from 1990 to 1994.
El Niño is a climate pattern that warms the central Pacific Ocean, often causing severe droughts in the Philippines.
